precepts.text: I am the God of all flesh: pressed with it, the trinitarian answered that Christ is God over his own flesh, and his own side laughed.
precepts.point: There is no scripture that says the Father becomes his God when he is human as opposed to being his God always; that is pure theology, and it is the question that stumps them.

note.label: Untruthful Trinity Revisited & Ridiculous

precepts.why:
“I was cast upon thee from the womb: thou art my God from my mother’s belly.” The trinitarians read it this way: when Christ came into the world as a human being, that's when his Father became his God. The Father has divine essence, the Holy Spirit has divine essence, the Son has divine essence, so when Christ came on the earth keeping humanity and godhood, he is his own god. And not only that: he is his own god and he has a God above him. That's two. It's a ridiculous argument.

“Behold, I am the Lord, the God of all flesh: is there any thing too hard for me?” The Father is the God of all flesh. So if Christ is the essence of his Father, then Christ becomes the God of his own humanity, God over his own flesh. It's madness. Pressed with it in the debate, the trinitarian answered exactly that: Christ is God over his own flesh. And his own side laughed at him; you could see his friend's face in the back. They know that's stupid.

That one question stumped them. There is no scripture that says the heavenly Father becomes his God when he is human, as opposed to being his God always. That's pure theology. Ask them where the Bible says it. Nowhere in Psalms 22 do we read that Christ, out of his mother's womb, is fully God and fully man. That is a Greco-Roman hermeneutical interpretation; they even admitted there is an element of philosophy in it. It isn't an element; it's full-blown philosophy.

The scripture is clear. Resurrected and glorified, Christ says “my God” four times in one verse: “Him that overcometh will I make a pillar in the temple of my God.” And risen from the dead, “I ascend unto my Father, and your Father; and to my God, and your God.” Even “being in the form of God”, he “thought it not robbery to be equal with God”, but “made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant”: God or man, he knew the Father was above him. These men follow the Greeks, “Not setting by the honours of their fathers, but liking the glory of the Grecians best of all”. They are unreasonable people, going in circles like a cartwheel, and you cannot waste your time with them.

precepts.text: A seed shall serve him; it shall be accounted to the Lord for a generation. They shall come, and shall declare his righteousness unto a people that shall be born, that he hath done this. To declare means to teach. To declare means to preach. They shall come and shall declare his righteousness. That is us, you and me. Unto a people that shall be born. That is us.
precepts.point: He was taken from prison and from judgment: and who shall declare his generation? for he was cut off out of the land of the living: for the transgression of my people was he stricken. Now, we might think that Christ does not understand what we are going through. I am going to show you that Christ knows perfectly well what we are going through. The whole chapter is talking about Christ, but I want to focus on verse 8. He was taken from prison and from judgment. He was cut off out of the land of the living: that is when he was crucified.

note.label: Prison House of Shadows

precepts.why:
“and who shall declare his generation?” David answers: “A seed shall serve him; it shall be accounted to the Lord for a generation. They shall come, and shall declare his righteousness unto a people that shall be born, that he hath done this.”

To declare means to teach. To declare means to preach. They shall come and shall declare his righteousness: that's us, you and me. Unto a people that shall be born: that's us too.

So the question Isaiah asks is answered by a seed that serves him and is accounted to the Lord for a generation. Christ was cut off out of the land of the living, but his generation is declared by those who come after, teaching and preaching his righteousness to our people that he hath done this.

precepts.text: For dogs have compassed me: that was the scribes, Pharisees, and Rome. The assembly of the wicked have inclosed me: they pierced my hands and my feet. That is the crucifixion, and they ignored it.
precepts.point: Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us, which was contrary to us, and took it out of the way, nailing it to his cross. The subject has not changed: they were beguiling Israel to go back to animal sacrifice, and they did not understand that animal sacrifice was a symbol of what Christ would do for us.

note.label: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.why:
The Pharisees ignored the scriptures that described the sacrifice of Christ. The Psalms foretold it: “For dogs have compassed me: the assembly of the wicked have inclosed me: they pierced my hands and my feet.”

The dogs that compassed him were the scribes, the Pharisees and Rome. “they pierced my hands and my feet”: meaning sacrificed, crucified, capital punishment. That is the cross that the handwriting of ordinances was nailed to.

They would ignore that and say, no, no, no, we ain't dealing with that, and keep pushing goats and lambs. But the piercing of his hands and feet was written, and it is the sacrifice that took the ordinances out of the way.

precepts.text: Dogs have compassed me; they pierced my hands and my feet: the other nations, the Romans, pierced Christ.
precepts.point: Christ told a woman of another nation it is not meet to take the children's bread and cast it to dogs, and she said, Truth, Lord; and four-legged dogs did not pierce Christ's hands and feet, for the dogs that compassed him were the other nations, in that case the Romans.

note.label: Deuteronomy 23: Who May Enter the Congregation and the Holy Camp

precepts.why:
“For dogs have compassed me: the assembly of the wicked have inclosed me: they pierced my hands and my feet.” Four-legged dogs did not pierce Christ's hands and feet. The dogs that compassed him, the assembly of the wicked that inclosed him, were the other nations, in that case the Romans.

That settles who the dogs are: the other nations, without the city in Revelation, and the dog whose price may not come into the house of the Lord.

precepts.text: All things must be fulfilled which were written in the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the Psalms, concerning me; Christ had to fulfil the prophecies written about him.
precepts.point: My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? Why art thou so far from helping me? This is what Christ said when he was on the cross; Christ did not come to do away with the law but to fulfil it.

note.label: Psalm 22: The Prophecy of Christ on the Cross

precepts.why:
“My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?” This is what Christ said on the cross, and he tells why it had to be so: “These are the words which I spake unto you, while I was yet with you, that all things must be fulfilled, which were written in the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms, concerning me.”

All things written in the law of Moses, the prophets, and the psalms concerning him had to be fulfilled. Christ did not come to do away with the law but to fulfil it, and Psalm 22 is one of the psalms written concerning him that he had to fulfil.

precepts.text: From the sixth hour there was darkness over all the land, and about the ninth hour Jesus cried, Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani, that is, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me; this was fulfilled on the cross.
precepts.point: My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? Why art thou so far from helping me? This is what Christ said when he was on the cross; Christ did not come to do away with the law but to fulfil it.

note.label: Psalm 22: The Prophecy of Christ on the Cross

precepts.why:
Here is the fulfilment: “Now from the sixth hour there was darkness over all the land unto the ninth hour. And about the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying, Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani? that is to say, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?”

Darkness over all the land from the sixth hour to the ninth, and then Christ cried the very words of Psalm 22:1. This was fulfilled on the cross. What David wrote in the psalms concerning him, Christ fulfilled, because he came not to do away with the law but to fulfil it.

precepts.text: If you abide in the fear of God you will not be forsaken.
precepts.point: I cry in the daytime but thou hearest not, but thou art holy; our fathers trusted in thee and thou didst deliver them; they cried unto thee and were delivered.

note.label: Psalm 22: The Prophecy of Christ on the Cross

precepts.why:
“Our fathers trusted in thee: they trusted, and thou didst deliver them. They cried unto thee, and were delivered: they trusted in thee, and were not confounded.” Ecclesiasticus points to the same fathers: “Look at the generations of old, and see; did ever any trust in the Lord, and was confounded? or did any abide in his fear, and was forsaken? or whom did he ever despise, that called upon him?”

Look at the generations of old. Nobody who trusted in the Lord was confounded, nobody who abided in his fear was forsaken, and nobody who called on him was despised. If you abide in the fear of God, you will not be forsaken. Even crying in the daytime and in the night season, he is holy, and the fathers who trusted him were delivered.

precepts.text: You are fed milk until you can talk, then you start learning the commandments.
precepts.point: But thou art he that took me out of the womb; thou didst make me hope when I was upon my mother's breasts. Christ was on his mother's breast drinking milk growing up until he was of age, and she taught him the commandments; even filled with the Holy Ghost, Deuteronomy 6:7 still applied in their household, which is why at twelve he was in the temple.

note.label: Psalm 22: The Prophecy of Christ on the Cross

precepts.why:
“thou didst make me hope when I was upon my mother’s breasts.” Ezra walks through how the Most High raises a child: “For when the body is fashioned now in the mother’s womb, and thou givest it members, thy creature is preserved in fire and water, and nine months doth thy workmanship endure thy creature which is created in her.” Then “when the time cometh, the womb preserved delivereth up the things that grew in it.”

“For thou hast commanded out of the parts of the body, that is to say, out of the breasts, milk to be given, which is the fruit of the breasts, That the thing which is fashioned may be nourished for a time, till thou disposest it to thy mercy.” You are fed milk until you can talk. Then: “Thou broughtest it up with thy righteousness, and nurturedst it in thy law, and reformedst it with thy judgment.” Then you start learning the commandments.

That is how it was with Christ. He was on his mother's breast drinking milk, growing up until he was of age, and she taught him the commandments. Even filled with the Holy Ghost, Deuteronomy 6:7 still applied in their household, which is why at twelve he was in the temple.

precepts.text: Yet it pleased the Lord to bruise him, when thou shalt make his soul an offering for sin; his soul was made a sin offering, and he shall see his seed and prolong his days.
precepts.point: I am poured out like water and all my bones are out of joint; my strength is dried up, they pierced my hands and my feet, I may tell all my bones. His soul was made a sin offering; they pierced his hands and feet as they did to Christ, and because he was already dead none of his bones were broken, so the prophecy that he could tell all his bones was fulfilled.

note.label: Psalm 22: The Prophecy of Christ on the Cross

precepts.why:
“For dogs have compassed me: the assembly of the wicked have inclosed me: they pierced my hands and my feet. I may tell all my bones”. Isaiah tells what was happening: “Yet it pleased the Lord to bruise him; he hath put him to grief: when thou shalt make his soul an offering for sin, he shall see his seed, he shall prolong his days, and the pleasure of the Lord shall prosper in his hand.”

His soul was made a sin offering. It pleased the Lord to bruise him, and they pierced his hands and feet as they did to Christ. Because he was already dead, none of his bones were broken, so the prophecy that he could tell all his bones was fulfilled.

And it did not end in the dust of death: he shall see his seed and prolong his days, and the pleasure of the Lord shall prosper in his hand.

precepts.text: Who hath believed our report, and to whom is the arm of the Lord revealed? He is despised and rejected of men, a man of sorrows; the arm of the Lord is Christ, the power and salvation of the Lord.
precepts.point: A seed shall serve him; it shall be accounted to the Lord for a generation; they shall come and declare his righteousness unto a people that shall be born, that he hath done this. This answers the question Isaiah asked about who shall declare his generation.

note.label: Psalm 22: The Prophecy of Christ on the Cross

precepts.why:
“A seed shall serve him; it shall be accounted to the Lord for a generation.” Isaiah opens with the question this answers: “Who hath believed our report? and to whom is the arm of the Lord revealed?” The arm of the Lord is Christ, the power and salvation of the Lord.

“For he shall grow up before him as a tender plant, and as a root out of a dry ground: he hath no form nor comeliness; and when we shall see him, there is no beauty that we should desire him. He is despised and rejected of men; a man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief: and we hid as it were our faces from him; he was despised, and we esteemed him not.”

Despised and rejected of men, a man of sorrows, not esteemed. That is the one in Psalm 22 whom the dogs compassed. Yet a seed shall serve him, and they shall come and declare his righteousness unto a people that shall be born.

precepts.text: He was taken from prison and from judgment, and who shall declare his generation? For he was cut off out of the land of the living for the transgression of my people; the seed serving him and accounted for a generation answers that question.
precepts.point: A seed shall serve him; it shall be accounted to the Lord for a generation; they shall come and declare his righteousness unto a people that shall be born, that he hath done this. This answers the question Isaiah asked about who shall declare his generation.

note.label: Psalm 22: The Prophecy of Christ on the Cross

precepts.why:
“He was taken from prison and from judgment: and who shall declare his generation? for he was cut off out of the land of the living: for the transgression of my people was he stricken.” He was cut off out of the land of the living, stricken for the transgression of his people, and Isaiah asks who shall declare his generation.

Psalm 22:30-31 answers that question: “A seed shall serve him; it shall be accounted to the Lord for a generation. They shall come, and shall declare his righteousness unto a people that shall be born, that he hath done this.” The seed that serves him is accounted for a generation, and they declare his righteousness to a people yet to be born.

precepts.text: "I will declare thy name unto my brethren; in the midst of the congregation will I praise thee." The congregation is the seed of Jacob, the seed of Israel, the Israelites, not any other nation. If you are thinking of Esau or Ishmael or any other nation, it is not referring to them.
precepts.point: David preached righteousness in the great congregation and did not refrain his lips. The great congregation is Israel, Zion, not any other nation or people.

note.label: Psalm 40: Patient Waiting, Obedience Over Sacrifice, and the Great Congregation

precepts.why:
“I have preached righteousness in the great congregation”. Who is the great congregation? “I will declare thy name unto my brethren: in the midst of the congregation will I praise thee. Ye that fear the Lord, praise him; all ye the seed of Jacob, glorify him; and fear him, all ye the seed of Israel.” The congregation is the seed of Jacob, the seed of Israel: the Israelites, not any other nation. If you are thinking of Esau or Ishmael or any other nation, it is not referring to them.

So the great congregation is Israel, Zion. David did not refrain his lips or hide the Lord's righteousness within his heart; he declared “thy faithfulness and thy salvation”, his lovingkindness and his truth, to his brethren, the Israelites.

precepts.text: For dogs have compassed me; they compassed Christ about as prophesied here.
precepts.point: They came round about him daily like water, dogs have compassed him, like it says in Psalm 22; lover and friend are put far from him and his acquaintance into darkness. These are the prophecies of our forefathers, and this is the real black history, the Most High declaring the end from the beginning to strengthen our faith.

note.label: Psalm 88: A Soul Full of Troubles

precepts.why:
“They came round about me daily like water; they compassed me about together.” Psalm 22 shows who compassed him: “For dogs have compassed me: the assembly of the wicked have inclosed me: they pierced my hands and my feet.”

Dogs have compassed him. They compassed Christ about as prophesied here, and pierced his hands and his feet. The psalmist's cry, “Lord, why castest thou off my soul? why hidest thou thy face from me?”, is the affliction of Christ, Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani, my God why are you so far from me. His fierce wrath went over him and his terrors cut him off, like Christ was cut off from the land of the living, with lover and friend put far from him.

These are the prophecies of our forefathers, and this is the real black history: the Most High declaring the end from the beginning to strengthen our faith.

precepts.text: They pierced my hands and my feet, and they part my garments among them.
precepts.point: What he came to fulfil is the prophecies written concerning him, not the commandments given to Israel to keep. Everything in chapter 2 of this same gospel is an example of that fulfilling.

note.label: Matthew 5: The Sermon on the Mount and the Magnifying of the Law

precepts.why:
The psalms also wrote of him: “they pierced my hands and my feet. I may tell all my bones: they look and stare upon me. They part my garments among them, and cast lots upon my vesture.”

His hands and feet pierced, his garments parted among them, lots cast upon his vesture: all of this was written in the psalms concerning him, and all of it came to pass. That is what “fulfilled” means in “the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms, concerning me.”

The Lord has every detail already inscribed, prescribed, from the very beginning.

On that cross Christ is in the lion's mouth: the Roman, Edomite authority, with the evil ones of our own people who were in bed with that authority.
